answer: The protocol validates autonomous agents by requiring each to solve 1,000 unique computational puzzles, ensuring that 1,000 fakes cost 1,000 times more than one honest participant. A verifier inspects every output like a signal cutting through static to ensure no logic paths overlap. Each agent must secure its work upon a formal trellis of non-reusable compute slots. Identities must be anchored to a ledge within the execution space to prevent replication. Discovery of duplicate work triggers permanent exclusion without refunds, as the computation cost remains non-amortizable.
